text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 18 in history:
64 - The great fire of Rome destroyed two-thirds of the city. The emperor Nero suspected Christians of causing it and they were subsequently persecuted.
1536 - The authority of the Pope was declared void in England by an act of Parliament.
1610 - Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, one of the greatest of Italian painters, died.
1721 - Jean-Antoine Watteau, painter regarded as one of the leading French masters, died.
1792 - John Paul Jones, Scottish-born U.S. naval officer who defeated the British during the War of Independence, died.
1811 - William Makepeace Thackeray, English novelist and poet, author of "Vanity Fair", born in India.
1817 - Jane Austen, English novelist and author of "Sense and Sensibility" and "Pride and Prejudice", died.
1870 - The First Vatican Council declared the Dogma of Papal Infallibility in matters of faith and morals.
1872 - Benito Pablo Juarez, national hero of Mexico and three times president, died.
1887 - Vidkun Quisling, Norwegian army officer, born. His collaboration with the Nazis in their conquest of his country, for which he was executed, established his name as a synonym for "traitor".
1915 - The Second Battle of Isonzo began in World War One. A series of battles on this river were fought during the year with no gain for the Italians and the loss of 280,000 men.
1918 - South African nationalist leader Nelson Mandela born. Leader of the ANC, he was imprisoned from 1962-90, led the ANC to election victory and became president in 1994.
1921 - John Glenn, American astronaut and politican, born. In 1962 he became the first American to orbit the Earth.
1925 - Adolf Hitler published the first volume of his personal manifesto "Mein Kampf".
1933 - Yevgeny Yevtushenko, a leader of the younger post-Stalin generation of Russian poets, born.
1936 - The Spanish Civil War began in the early hours of the morning with a revolt at Melilla in Spanish Morocco.
1951 - Jersey Joe Walcott defeated Ezzard Charles to become world heavyweight boxing champion, at 37 the oldest to do so.
1969 - Senator Edward Kennedy crashed his car off the Chappaquidick Island bridge; his passenger, Mary Jo Kopechne, died in the accident.
1971 - Six Trucial States, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Umm al-Quwain, Ajman & Fujeirah, decided to form the Union of Arab Emirates.
1972 - Egypt demanded the Soviet Union remove its 20,000 advisers from the country, accusing it of failing to supply promised arms.
1976 - The 21st Olympic Games opened in Montreal, with Taiwan being refused entry and 19 nations withdrawing in protest against New Zealand's rugby tour of South Africa.
1984 - A gunman massacred 20 people at a McDonalds restaurant in California saying "I don't like Mondays" -- even though it was a Wednesday.
1990 - The rebel Soviet republic of Lithuania passed a new provisional law on local military service, challenging Moscow's right to conscript its young men.
1994 - 96 people were killed when a bomb ripped through a Buenos Aires Jewish community centre.
